old: a strange Western phrase. Don't human beings already do that?
new: a strange Western phrase. People here are like, "Don't human beings already do that?"
why: trace T1: the question read as the narrator's own claim and lost "people assume"; it is theirs now, and still the break

old: etc. etc. all get taken care of by the extended family and local memory, in addition to whatever formal systems there might be.
new: etc. etc. often get taken care of by the extended family and local memory, in addition to the formal systems.
why: trace T2: the published "often" (Emulate's "all" made it always) and formal systems that exist (Emulate's "whatever formal systems there might be" left open that there are none)

old: In the villages and families I've spent time around, a lot of the things we think we have to "re-invent" to form intentional communities are simply the way things are done. Land, childcare,
new: In the villages and families I've spent time around, land, childcare,
why: trace T2 and the stance check, two readers: "a lot of the things we think we have to "re-invent" ... are simply the way things are done" told the reader the villages already do it all and there is little left to build; the published says only what often passes through the family; variant s (v5-variants.json) keeps a softer form of the sentence

old: And can you blame them? Families that used to share almost everything are now more reliant on cash and individual opportunities.
new: So what about the families? The ones that used to share almost everything are now more reliant on cash and individual opportunities.
why: trace T5 and the stance check, two readers: "And can you blame them?" was a verdict on the young people's choices the published never gives; the break is now a question the published sentence answers

old: Even in Dakar, I see things like this spray painted on walls:
new: Even in Dakar, I found this graffiti on a wall:
why: trace T3: one find, as published ("I found graffiti reading"); "I see things like this" made it a common sight

old: I can't just praise the virtues of community and ignore the people who have to hide who they are to survive in it, or leave.
new: I'm not going to praise communal belonging and ignore the people who have to hide who they are to survive it, or leave.
why: trace T3: "can't" made a choice an inability (the published "I don't want to"; "I don't want to" opening a stance is the linter's O20, so his refusal is "I'm not going to"); the published "communal belonging" and "survive it", the belonging the next paragraph's "belong without pretending" rests on

old: It's possible for a society to be incredibly spiritually alive, generous, funny and super communal, while at the same time being extremely cruel to those who break its social categories.
new: It's possible for a society to be spiritually alive, generous, funny and super communal, while still becoming cruel to those who break its social categories.
why: trace T4: the published "still becoming" cruel (Emulate's "being" made it simply cruel), and no "incredibly" or "extremely" the published never gives

old: it depends on whether you're allowed to belong without pretending.
new: it all depends on whether you're allowed to belong without pretending.
why: trace T4: the published "Everything depends"

old: One other shadow side of the forgiving social culture here is that people will go to pretty funny lengths to avoid confrontation.
new: One other shadow side of the otherwise forgiving social culture here is that people may go to great lengths to avoid confrontation.
why: trace T4: the published "otherwise" (forgiving but for the cruelty just described) and "may"; "pretty funny" was a new opinion, and "great lengths" is the published "so thoroughly"

old: Of course, the old ways here are changing. Young people want to move to the city, get a job, get a phone, eat imported food, be part of the wider world, etc. (some young men even make the dangerous journey by sea to Europe).
new: Of course, the old communal ways here are changing. Young people move to the city, get a job, get a phone, eat imported food, become part of the wider world, etc. (some of the men even make the dangerous journey by sea to Europe).
why: trace T5: the published "communal" patterns; they do these things (not only "want to"); men, not only young men

old: Then there's the so-called "Black Tax," a legacy of the old communal system: if you've got any money at all, you're expected to share it with your parents, your siblings, to pay school fees,
new: Then there's the so-called "Black Tax," a strange legacy of the old communal system: if you've got any money at all, you're expected to share it with your parents, your siblings, your cousins, to pay school fees,
why: trace T6: the published "strange" survival, and "cousins", the extended family the obligation reaches (the list's "etc." came after the costs); "housed and protected" stay out by Joel's list rule (2026-10-03, 10-07), so the paragraph keeps one list of three (E125), recorded in make_v3

old: So why not share in return? It was the most natural thing to do, and that's how the whole organism survived (nobody thought of it as charity).
new: So why not share in return? That's how the whole organism survived (it wasn't charity).
why: trace T6: "the most natural thing to do" was Emulate's new opinion; the published says what sharing was, not what everyone thought ("it wasn't charity")

old: The problem is that it can be very soul destroying in today's world. The obligation is still there, but most people no longer live close enough to share land, work, childcare, food etc. and feel part of a larger whole, while whoever earns the cash
new: The problem is that it can be soul destroying in today's world. The obligation is still there, but a lot of the communal life that held it up is gone (people don't fully share the land, the work, the childcare, the food and the daily belonging like they used to), while whoever earns the cash
why: trace T6: no "very"; the published communal life that supported the obligation, "much of" it gone and the rest "no longer fully shared" (Emulate's "most people no longer live close enough" gave distance as the cause, which the published never says), with its "daily belonging"

old: So the ancestral ethic carries on inside the individualistic cash economy, keeping people alive but gnawing at both sides.
new: The ancestral ethic carries on inside the individualistic cash economy, where it can keep people alive but gnaw at both sides.
why: trace T6: "So" made it follow from the relatives' dependence; the published "can"

old: It's also one of the thorny boundary issues of living without money inside a money-based society.
new: It's also the thorny boundary issue of living without money inside a money-based society.
why: trace T7: the published names the boundary problem, not one of several

old: That doesn't mean going back to individuals working for wages and bringing them into the commune, but
new: That doesn't mean going back to individual wages inside the commune, but
why: trace T7: the published rules out wages inside the commune; "individuals working for wages and bringing them into the commune" ruled out the outside work the next paragraph allows

old: Another aspect of outside work is that it's not just money you're bringing into the commune.
new: Another aspect of outside work, even before there's a common purse, is that it's not just money you're bringing into the commune.
why: trace T7: the published "even before a common purse"

old: different loyalties, different consumption habits etc. etc.
new: different loyalties, and often different consumption habits etc. etc.
why: trace T7: the published "often"

old: In the first stage, where some people work outside and contribute an agreed share, it's really important that they can't use the money to buy their way out of communal work,
new: In the first stage, where people working outside should contribute an agreed share, it's really important that they can't use the money to buy their way out of everyday communal work,
why: trace T7: the published "should" contribute, and "ordinary" communal work

old: It's also important that outside jobs don't drain the energy and skills out of the people who could be building the communal livelihoods. Otherwise the commune will never develop a common purse, and it will stay a dormitory for the money economy.
new: It's also important that the group notices when outside jobs start draining the people and skills it needs to build the communal livelihoods. Otherwise the commune will stay a dormitory for the money economy instead of moving toward a common purse.
why: trace T7: the group's job to notice, the people and skills it needs (Emulate's "who could be building" made them only available), and the published "instead of moving toward a common purse" (Emulate's "never develop" was absolute)

old: used to try to stop their young people from emigrating, which is a version of the same problem.
new: used to try to stop their young people from leaving, which is a version of the same outside-work problem.
why: trace T8: the published "leaving" (migration need not cross a border); the cold read: "the same problem" could be the money owed to relatives or the outside jobs, so it is named (the published "this" is the outside-work boundary)

old: There's knowledge in the living villages that no book can give you. And by the way, if you visit, remember they're people, not museums.
new: There's still knowledge in the living villages that no book can give you. But if you visit, remember they're people, not museums.
why: trace T9: the published "still", and "but": the people are the counterweight to the knowledge, not an aside

old: So be respectful, go wanting to contribute, learn some of the language, and don't expect
new: So be respectful, contribute something, learn the language, and don't expect
why: trace T9: the published asks for a contribution and the language, not the wish or some of it

old: getting my residency here was pretty cheap and straightforward.
new: getting my residency in Sénégal was pretty cheap and straightforward.
why: trace T9: the published names the country, and "the country's" ideal two sentences on needs it

old: and they won't let me pay rent! I know, I'm lucky.
new: and they won't let me pay rent! Can you believe it?
why: trace T9: "I'm lucky" was a new self-assessment; the break claims nothing now
